source_fields.formulation: One learner must adapt to all comparator paths without knowing path length in advance. Losses are exponentially concave, path length is Euclidean, and the complete current function is revealed after acting.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: The learner acts in the same nonempty compact convex set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$ each round and is compared simultaneously with every comparator path $u_{1:T}\in W^T$. Losses are differentiable and exp-concave on $W$: $$\operatorname{diam}_2(W)\le D,\qquad e^{-\eta f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }W\text{ is concave},\qquad \|\nabla f_t(w)\|_2\le G\quad(\forall t,\ w\in W).$$ The upper bound holds for each admissible realized loss sequence; the recorded lower bound uses a sequence fixed before interaction. For dimension optimality, $D,G,\eta$ are fixed independently of $d,T$. Precisely, exp-concavity means that for each round $t$, the map $x\mapsto\exp(-\eta f_t(x))$ is concave on the stated feasible set. It concerns the full action variable, with the norm and gradient bounds specified here.

components.description: $T$ sequential rounds, or $T$ rounds per task

$T$ is the online horizon. The algorithm covering the full stated range uses $O(\log T)$ loss evaluations, gradient evaluations, and Euclidean projections per round, including the internal work of the exp-concave branch. The following expressions give total dense spectral/projection arithmetic and storage, respectively; storage counts real numbers, not bits: $$\text{arithmetic cost}=O\!\left(T\bigl(d^3+C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)\bigr)\log^2(2T)\right),\qquad \text{storage}=O\!\left(d^2\log^2(2T)\right).$$ This specification provides full-function feedback. The single-gradient-at-the-action variant is a separate information contract, so these resources cannot be described as one gradient call per round. Exploration, initialization, and identification count toward the online budget. Oracle calls, arithmetic, communication rounds/bits, and memory remain separate resources; no optimal arithmetic or bit complexity is asserted.

cost.arithmetic: O(T(d^3+C_proj(d)) log^2(2T)) dense spectral curved cost

source_fields.complete_expression: The upper bound is deterministic and holds pathwise: the same algorithm works simultaneously for every admissible loss sequence and comparator path. The lower bound considers the expression below, with expectation only over learner randomness. The quantity $P$ is an analytical comparator budget, not a known algorithm input. $$\inf_{\mathcal A}\ \sup_{\substack{f_{1:T}\ \text{admissible},\ u_{1:T}\in W^T\\ P_T^{(2)}(u)\le P}}\ \mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\!\left[\operatorname{Reg}_T(u)\right].$$
aggregation_order: The upper bound is pathwise and deterministic: one algorithm satisfies it for every admissible loss sequence and comparator path simultaneously. In the lower-bound criterion below, expectation is only over learner randomness. The quantity $P$ is an analysis budget for the comparator class, not a known algorithm input.
$$\inf_{\mathcal A}\ \sup_{\substack{f_{1:T}\ \text{admissible},\ u_{1:T}\in W^T\\ P_T^{(2)}(u)\le P}}\ \mathbb E_{\mathcal A}\!\left[\operatorname{Reg}_T(u)\right].$$
